source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Carrying fairly little relationship much to the client's overall coagulation status, despite being given specifically for this exact clinical reason","B":"May provide some benefit if vitamin K deficiency is contributing, but liver disease-related coagulopathy often results primarily from impaired synthetic function rather than vitamin K deficiency alone","C":"Fully correcting the elevated INR reading in essentially every affected case, since liver disease-related coagulopathy is thought to stem mainly from a simple lack of vitamin K","D":"Being considered contraindicated in most clients who happen to have any form of underlying chronic liver disease present, regardless of severity or INR value"}}
source_row.rationale: Vitamin K may provide some benefit if deficiency is contributing to the elevated INR, but liver disease-related coagulopathy often results primarily from impaired hepatic synthetic function of clotting factors rather than vitamin K deficiency alone, so vitamin K administration may not fully correct the INR in significant liver disease.
